chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The distance between one side of the well of al-Ma'tin and the other is forty cubits, and the distance between one side of the well of al-Nadhih and the other is sixty cubits, and the distance between one side of the spring (source) and the other — meaning the channel — is five hundred cubits. And the road, when its owners dispute over it, its boundary is seven cubits."
ai.seo_question: What are the prescribed measurements for water rights and road boundaries in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides precise jurisprudential metrics for water rights (*haqq al-ma'*), distinguishing between the ownership extent of wells, cattle-drinking spots, and irrigation channels, while also defining the standard width of roads in cases of dispute. It reflects the early Islamic legal tradition's emphasis on quantifiable property boundaries to prevent conflict, a principle deeply rooted in Shia fiqh regarding communal and private resource management. The specific measurements serve as a foundational reference for *fiqh al-mu'amalat* (jurisprudence of transactions) concerning natural resources.
